brief: Goldman Sachs argues S&P 500 earnings are elevated but not in a bubble. EPS grew 51% in Q2 2026 and 26% over the past four quarters, well above trend and the market's historical link to GDP growth, prompting investor concern about an earnings bubble. Three temporary drivers explain the over-earning. AI infrastructure capex is boosting earnings today, but its 11pp tailwind fades to a marginal drag by 2028 as depreciation rises. Semiconductor gross margins near record highs (80% for memory) should plateau in 2027-2028. Roughly $150bn of Q2 mega-cap "other income" from private equity stakes added 12% to EPS and should shrink sharply in 2027. As these fade, Goldman forecasts EPS growth decelerating to 11% in both 2027 ($415) and 2028 ($460), supported by 2.1-2.3% GDP growth and easing oil prices, with AI productivity gains only gradually offsetting the capex slowdown. The 19x forward P/E looks fair against history, and a 24% ROE (a record) justifies it, so earnings growth rather than multiple expansion should keep driving 3/6/12-month price targets of 8000/8300/8700.
